risks: model ranking does not hold across windows
only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~44% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. Predictability is middling — structured signal and irregular noise are balanced. The series reads as non-stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (1 points, ~1% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.072), which favours a robust combination.

test a weighted combination using a meta‑model to learn weights across series; this is a new weighting scheme not yet tried.

Test a weighted combination using the top‑k per‑horizon handle w6, which has a higher concentration (0.073) than w5, to see if a slightly different per‑horizon averaging improves over the current leader.
use a subset of the best models (k=7) to reduce correlation and try inverse_error weighting on that subset.
test a softmax‑negative‑error weighted combo on the reduced, decorrelated pool4 to reduce variance and exploit strong seasonality.

Series context: trend strength 0.9999 and seasonal strength 0.9999; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.072); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 3.297.
